\paragraph{Prompt template.}
For NER, we use a structured prompt:
\begin{quote}
\small
\texttt{System:} You are an expert in Named Entity Recognition.\\
\texttt{User:} Extract all named entities from the following text. Output as JSON.\\
Text: \texttt{\{input\_text\}}\\
Entity types: \texttt{\{schema\_types\}}
\end{quote}
RE follows the same structure with ``Relation Extraction'' and relation type lists substituted accordingly.

\paragraph{Constrained decoding.}
Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar-based JSON schema enforcement \cite{willard2023guided}, which constrains outputs to valid entity/relation structures matching the target schema.
This eliminates format errors but may compress per-sample diversity by restricting the output space.\footnote{SciERC training used \texttt{enable\_thinking=True} (LLaMA Factory 0.9.4 default), injecting empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks (4--5 tokens) into each training response with loss computation; CoNLL and WNUT explicitly set \texttt{enable\_thinking=False}. Constrained decoding at inference time enforces JSON-only output, suppressing thinking tokens. See \S\ref{sec:setup} and Limitations for discussion of this confound.}

\section{Thinking Token Impact Analysis}\label{app:thinking_token}

Qwen3-8B's SciERC checkpoint was trained with empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks prepended to each response (\S\ref{sec:setup}).
We quantify the potential impact on LP scores through three complementary arguments.

\paragraph{LP shift magnitude.}
Empty thinking tokens (mean 4.5 per sample) constitute 2.1\% of tokens on SciERC.
The estimated LP shift is 0.001 nats per token (2.68\% of the median within-instance LP range of 0.041 nats).
Because all samples share identical thinking-token LP offsets, cumulative LP rankings are invariant; mean LP changes selection for ${<}1.5\%$ of instances.

\paragraph{Constant prefix cancellation.}
All $N$ samples within an instance share the same prompt and, under constrained decoding, the same absence of thinking tokens at inference time.
Any LP bias from the training-time thinking prefix is therefore a near-constant additive shift across all candidates within an instance, leaving within-instance LP \textit{rankings} unchanged.

\paragraph{CoNLL control group.}
CoNLL and WNUT-17 checkpoints were trained without thinking tokens (\texttt{enable\_thinking=False}).
If thinking tokens caused LP compression on SciERC, CoNLL should exhibit lower tied fractions.
Instead, CoNLL shows \textit{higher} tied fractions at both temperatures (86.8\% at $T{=}1.0$, 95.8\% at $T{=}0.7$) than SciERC (60.3\% at $T{=}1.0$), directly contradicting the thinking-token hypothesis.

\section{Log-Probability Score Compression}\label{app:logprob_ties}

Under constrained decoding, log-probability scores are severely compressed within instances, limiting per-sample discrimination (Table~\ref{tab:logprob_ties}, Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}).
The median within-instance LP range is only 0.041 nats---below the $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ threshold used throughout, providing data-driven justification for this cutoff rather than an arbitrary choice.
At $\varepsilon{=}0.05$, 60.3\% of instances ($n{=}529$, excluding empty gold annotations) have a within-sample range below the threshold, and 75\% of pairwise comparisons are effective ties ($|\Delta|{<}0.026$).
The CDF rises smoothly with no cliff or discontinuity (Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}), confirming that compression is a pervasive regime rather than a bimodal split.
This compression is stable across seeds: seed${=}456$ yields median LP range${=}0.040$ nats and tied fraction${=}62.2\%$ (vs.\ seed${=}42$: $0.041$ nats, $60.3\%$).
Seed~456 uses a different subtask flag (joint vs.\ ner for seeds 42 and 123); the LP distributions are statistically indistinguishable (median LP: 8.37 vs.\ 8.20 nats; Mann--Whitney $p{=}0.55$), confirming that the subtask change does not affect compression.
For comparison, SJ has only 12.5\% tied instances at the same threshold---SJ's advantage over LP for selection is one of score resolution, not information content.

\section{MBR Decoding and Task-Specific Interactions}\label{app:mbr_discussion}

\paragraph{Connection to MBR decoding.}
Our selection strategies instantiate minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, muller2021understanding}: each selects $\hat{y} = \arg\max_{y_i} \sum_{j \neq i} U(y_i, y_j)$ with utility $U$ defined by SJ, EM, or entity overlap.
Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high} and its extension to summarization, code generation, and captioning \cite{jinnai2024mbr}, all variants fail here because the utility functions correlate with F1 at the instance level but not within a single instance---the mathematical essence of the correlation-selection gap.
\citet{eikema2025structured} study structure-conditional MBR decoding and find that standard utility functions degrade on structured outputs---consistent with our finding that consensus-proximity selection fails in IE despite its success in machine translation.

\paragraph{Task-specific decoding interactions.}
The free-form ablation reveals divergent behavior across tasks.
On RE, LP selection flips from $-0.68$~pp (constrained) to $+1.69$~pp (free-form; preliminary, single RE benchmark), a reversal that spans all 7 relation types and is driven by selective variance reallocation ($p{<}0.0001$).
The win/loss ratio shifts from 36:59 (constrained) to 45:45 (free-form), with the gains concentrated on relation-dense instances (mean 3.3 gold relations).
This interaction does not generalize to NER, where selection remains negligible under both regimes.
This ablation uses a single seed (seed${=}42$); whether the RE reversal replicates across seeds and generalizes to other RE benchmarks warrants further investigation.
The non-tied subset ($n{=}210$) is partially reshuffled under free-form decoding: Jaccard similarity between the constrained and free-form non-tied sets is 0.472, indicating that 87 instances newly gain LP discrimination while others lose it, yielding a $3{\times}$ increase in within-instance LP range for the newly non-tied subset.
Despite this reshuffling, aggregate NER selection gains remain negligible---score compression is not a fixed property of specific instances but rather a pervasive regime that shifts across instances without producing net selection improvement.
Free-form decoding also slightly improves quality estimation (NER VC $\rho$: 0.379$\to$0.409), though this does not translate to selection gains.

\section{LP Selection Failure Stability}\label{app:lp_failure_stability}

We analyze RE LP selection failures across three random seeds (constrained decoding, $N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, Qwen3-8B) to assess whether failures are systematic or stochastic.

\paragraph{Pairwise overlap.}
LP selection failures (instances where LP-selected F1 $<$ greedy F1) show moderate cross-seed stability: the average pairwise Jaccard similarity is 0.42 (range: 0.38--0.46), indicating that failures are partially systematic---driven by instance complexity---but not fully deterministic.
The 3-way intersection contains 34 instances (27.9\% of any-seed failures), confirming a stable failure core.

\paragraph{Instance complexity drives failure.}
Table~\ref{tab:stable_failures} stratifies instances by failure stability.
Stable failures (all 3 seeds) involve more gold relations (2.12 vs.\ 1.62 for never-fail instances) and higher greedy F1 (0.688 vs.\ 0.429), indicating that LP mis-selects on instances where the model already performs well---precisely the instances where selection would be most valuable.
Failure rate increases monotonically with gold relation count: 4.3\% at 1 relation, 20.7\% at 3 relations, 26.2\% at 6 relations.

\bottomrule

\end{table}

\paragraph{Flip instances.}
Only 5 RE instances with gold relations flip from LP failure (constrained) to LP success (free-form), with mean gold relation count 3.67 (well above the population mean of 1.86).
These instances show large constrained LP errors ($\Delta{=}{-}0.430$) that reverse under free-form decoding ($\Delta{=}{+}0.503$), but their rarity (5/397) confirms that the RE selection flip is driven by aggregate variance reallocation rather than systematic instance-level correction.

\section{Cross-Dataset OOD Analysis}\label{app:ood}

To test whether confidence signals generalize under domain shift, we evaluate models on out-of-distribution data: a SciERC-trained model applied to CoNLL instances (wider$\to$narrower schema) and vice versa (Table~\ref{tab:ood}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-dataset OOD quality estimation (Spearman $\rho$, Qwen3-8B, $N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, seed${=}42$). SciERC$\to$CoNLL: SciERC-trained model on CoNLL instances ($n{=}2756$). CoNLL$\to$SciERC: CoNLL-trained model on SciERC instances ($n{=}529$, excluded from conclusions due to catastrophic model failure). In-domain $\rho$ from Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation} (same model, same seed). \textsuperscript{***}$p{<}0.001$, \textsuperscript{*}$p{<}0.05$.}
\label{tab:ood}
\begin{tabular}{l ccc ccc}
\toprule

\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-7}
Signal & $\rho$ & In-dom. & $\Delta$ & $\rho$ & In-dom. & $\Delta$ \\
\midrule
VC & .469\textsuperscript{***} & .379 & +.090 & +.105\textsuperscript{*} & .379 & $-$.274 \\
SJ & .378\textsuperscript{***} & .360 & +.018 & $-$.186\textsuperscript{***} & .360 & $-$.546 \\
EM & .300\textsuperscript{***} & .295 & +.005 & $-$.202\textsuperscript{***} & .295 & $-$.497 \\
FK & .285\textsuperscript{***} & .267 & +.018 & $-$.070 & .267 & $-$.337 \\
LP & .246\textsuperscript{***} & .205 & +.041 & $-$.152\textsuperscript{***} & .205 & $-$.357 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Wider-to-narrower schema transfer.}
When the SciERC-trained model (6 NER types) is applied to CoNLL (4 types), all signals remain significant ($p{<}0.001$) and structural signals improve over their in-domain levels (same model, seed${=}42$, $N{=}8$; in-domain $\rho$ from Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}): VC reaches $\rho{=}0.469$ (in-domain $0.379$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.090$), SJ $\rho{=}0.378$ (in-domain $0.360$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.018$), and FK $\rho{=}0.285$ (in-domain $0.267$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.018$).
The wider training schema subsumes CoNLL's narrower schema, so the model produces reasonable outputs even out-of-domain (greedy F1${=}0.522$), and structural signals benefit from the simpler target schema's reduced output ambiguity.

\paragraph{Narrower-to-wider schema transfer (excluded).}
The reverse direction is excluded from our conclusions due to catastrophic model failure, not signal failure.
The CoNLL-trained model recognizes only 4 news entity types (PER, ORG, LOC, MISC) and has no relation extraction capability; when applied to SciERC's 6 scientific entity types and 7 relation types, the model cannot produce meaningful structured outputs (greedy NER F1${=}0.009$, RE F1${=}0.001$).
Under this regime, most signals flip to negative or near-zero correlations (Table~\ref{tab:ood}); only VC retains weak positive correlation ($\rho{=}0.105$, $p{=}0.016$).
These negative correlations reflect the model systematically generating confident but incorrect outputs---a capability failure analogous to WNUT-17 (\S\ref{sec:qe_results}), not evidence against signal utility.

\paragraph{Asymmetry interpretation.}
The directional asymmetry is driven by schema coverage: wider$\to$narrower preserves signal utility because the SciERC model's 6-type schema subsumes CoNLL's 4 types, while narrower$\to$wider fails because the CoNLL model lacks the entity and relation types required by SciERC.
This extends the capability boundary identified on WNUT-17 to the domain-shift setting: confidence signals require sufficient model capability as a prerequisite, and results from the CoNLL$\to$SciERC direction should not be interpreted as evidence of signal degradation under domain shift.

\section{Verbalized Confidence}\label{app:verbalized_confidence}

We evaluate verbalized confidence (VerbConf) as a second per-sample signal following \citet{tian2023calibration}: after generating each structured output, the model is prompted to rate its confidence on a 1--10 scale.
Table~\ref{tab:verbconf} reports quality estimation and selection results.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small

\label{tab:verbconf}
\begin{tabular}{l cc cc}
\toprule

\cmidrule(lr){2-3} \cmidrule(lr){4-5}
Metric & VerbConf & LP & VerbConf & LP \\
\midrule
$\rho$ & 0.297 & 0.205 & 0.337 & 0.316 \\
AUROC & 0.681 & 0.578 & 0.747 & 0.753 \\
Selection F1 & 0.620 & 0.647 & 0.889 & 0.904 \\
$\Delta$ vs.\ greedy & $-$2.45\,pp & $+$0.2\,pp & $-$1.93\,pp & $-$0.77\,pp \\
\midrule
Mean score & 8.58\,/\,10 & --- & 9.24\,/\,10 & --- \\
Parse fail rate & 0.26\% & --- & 0\% & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Severe overconfidence.}
VerbConf exhibits extreme score compression: mean confidence is 8.58/10 on SciERC (greedy F1${=}0.645$) and 9.24/10 on CoNLL (greedy F1${=}0.904$), with most scores concentrated in the 8--10 range.
This compression is more severe than LP (which spans a 0.041-nat median range), confirming that score compression is a general property of model self-assessment, not an artifact of log-probability computation.

\paragraph{QE--selection decoupling.}
VerbConf achieves higher $\rho$ than LP on both datasets (SciERC: 0.297 vs.\ 0.205; CoNLL: 0.337 vs.\ 0.316) and competitive AUROC (SciERC: 0.681 vs.\ 0.578; CoNLL: 0.747 vs.\ 0.753), yet yields the worst selection among all signals ($\Delta{=}{-}2.45$~pp on SciERC, $-1.93$~pp on CoNLL).
This dissociation further demonstrates the correlation-selection gap: a signal can rank instances by expected quality without being able to discriminate candidates within an instance.
The AUROC--$\rho$ decoupling on CoNLL (LP leads AUROC at 0.753 while VerbConf leads $\rho$ at 0.337) reflects differing sensitivity to binary vs.\ ordinal discrimination.

# ARR Reviewer Guidelines: Key Evaluation Criteria

## What Reviewers Should Evaluate

Reviewers assess papers across multiple dimensions:

**Soundness**: Technical correctness and methodological rigor. Reviews must justify low soundness scores with specific evidence from the paper text.

**Excitement**: Personal interest level, kept separate from soundness. "You may find the work sound, but not something that is interesting for you personally."

**Overall Recommendation**: Composite judgment reflecting soundness, excitement, novelty, and potential impact for the field.

## Core Review Standards

### Specificity (I1)
Reviews must be concrete. Rather than "The paper is missing relevant references," specify "The paper is missing references X, Y, Z." Generic criticisms lack actionable value.

### Professional Tone (I4)
"A good review should be professional and neutral, if not kind." Sarcasm and dismissiveness harm reviewer-author relationships and contribute to peer review dysfunction.

### Score Alignment (I3)
Scores must correspond to review content. Low soundness ratings require documented technical problems; without justification, scores suggest unconscious bias.

## Common Review Problems to Avoid

The guidelines flag 17 problematic heuristics (H1-H17), including:

- **H1/H2**: Dismissing results as "obvious" or contradicting personal expectations
- **H5**: Demanding SOTA results when papers claim other contributions
- **H6**: Bias against negative/null results
- **H13**: Requiring experiments beyond the paper's stated claims
- **H16**: Listing acknowledged limitations as weaknesses

## Negative Results & Reproducibility

Negative findings deserve publication. "The bias towards publishing only positive results is a known problem in many fields, and contributes to hype and overclaiming."

Reproducibility assessment (M2) evaluates whether sufficient details exist to replicate experiments—not whether reviewers personally run code.

## Specific NLP Paper Issues

The guidelines identify problematic practices:

- **M1**: Using LLMs as evaluators without validating their reliability
- **R1**: P-hacking, unreported hyperparameter tuning, unfairly weak baselines
- **R5**: Missing statistical significance tests or effect sizes
- **G5**: Fabricated or misrepresented citations (increasingly from LLM summaries)

## Review Updates After Author Response

Reviewers must acknowledge author responses. Either explain why rebuttals remain unconvincing or update scores if concerns were addressed—simply ignoring responses is considered poor practice.

- Experiments span two model families at multiple scales (Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B with 4B and 3B ablations), using N=8 as primary and N=16 for supplementary analysis across 3 seeds

Now I'm reviewing the assessment criteria: soundness, excitement, and overall assessment on 5-point scales with half-point increments, plus reviewer confidence and reproducibility ratings. I'm also verifying the references—44 entries with 66 citations total.

Most citations check out, though 3 entries aren't indexed (likely preprints like hobelsberger2025systematic, lightman2024verify, venktesh2025trust) and there are 3 author formatting mismatches, but no fabricated citations detected.

Now I'm drafting the review along the dimensions of methodological rigor, experimental design, and statistical validity. The critical issue I'm identifying is that RE coverage is too narrow—the paper relies solely on SciERC for relation extraction evidence, yet frames the correlation-selection gap as a universal problem across structured IE. The title and abstract don't adequately qualify this limitation, and the claims about LLM-based information extraction need stronger empirical grounding across multiple benchmarks.

I'm also flagging the ε=0.05 threshold for tied fractions as potentially data-driven post-hoc selection. The appendix justifies it by noting the median LP range falls below this cutoff, but that's circular reasoning—the threshold appears chosen to validate the median. Table 11's ε sweep shows the strongest p-value at exactly ε=0.05, which suggests optimization rather than principled selection. The experiments.tex footnote clarifies that ε only applies to selection analysis, not quality estimation, which is good, but the selection findings still hinge on this threshold choice.

The causal claim about LP compression being model-dependent needs more scrutiny.  The free-form ablation only covers SciERC NER with Qwen3-8B across four seeds, then extends to CoNLL NER, yet the RE results actually show LP selection working under free-form decoding—contradicting the "task-intrinsic" framing for relation extraction. The ablation also doesn't explore whether other decoding strategies like nucleus sampling or temperature adjustments would shift compression patterns.

The scale range of 3B–8B is too narrow to support the claim that task difficulty drives the gap. The paper asserts this as the primary driver within the tested range across two model families, but that's a strong causal conclusion from limited scale coverage.

With only three seeds, the stability claims feel overstated—the ranking stability metric σ≤0.026 comes with substantial uncertainty, and Kendall's W=1.000 with just three observations isn't particularly informative since any consistent ranking would produce that result. There's also a notable asymmetry in how empty-gold instances are filtered: CoNLL has 20.2% filtered out versus SciERC's 4.0%, which could meaningfully skew the results.

The Qwen3-8B thinking token explanation on SciERC would be more convincing with a direct control—retraining SciERC with thinking disabled and comparing—rather than relying on the CoNLL control group, which conflates the thinking token issue with differences in task difficulty and entity types. The selection analysis also uses macro F1, treating all instances equally regardless of entity or relation count, so micro F1 or entity-weighted metrics might show different patterns. One more thing: the "greedy" baseline is actually a temperature-1.0 sample rather than a deterministic argmax, which is a confusing naming choice.

The paper misses several natural baselines like combining LP with consistency signals, weighted ensemble approaches, or simple heuristics such as selecting the sample with highest entity overlap to majority vote. On the statistical side, using Fisher combined p-values across seeds is problematic because the test instances are identical across seeds—the same instances just have different sampled outputs—so the per-seed tests aren't independent, which could artificially inflate the combined p-value.

Actually, reconsidering this: the samples are independent across seeds due to different random states, but the test sets overlap completely, creating positive correlation between test statistics. Under positive dependence, Fisher's method becomes conservative, making it harder to find positive results rather than easier, so this actually works against finding effects rather than inflating them. The TOST equivalence testing is well-executed with external anchors and proper circularity acknowledgment, and the bootstrap confidence intervals with 10,000 resamples and pairwise comparisons are solid.

The Bonferroni correction note correctly identifies that uncorrected tests are appropriate for negative results, which is methodologically sound. Looking at the overall picture: this is a thorough paper with strong statistical methodology, comprehensive ablations, and a novel finding about the correlation-selection gap that has practical value. The main limitations are the narrow focus on NER for the core finding and the restricted scale range, which constrains how much I can generalize from the results. I'm settling on this as a solid 3.5 — the work is well-executed and the core insight is interesting, but some of the broader claims push beyond what the evidence fully supports. I'm reconsidering the guidelines around negative results — they explicitly discourage bias against them, and this finding does have practical value for practitioners. I'll adjust my scores to be fairer: keeping soundness at 3.5 and excitement at 3, but raising the overall to 3.5 with high confidence, then draft the full review.

## Must-Fix 问题（影响接收决定）

**N1** [critical] RE 覆盖不足与 claim scope 不匹配
- 具体位置：Title ("LLM-Based Information Extraction"), Abstract line 3 ("NER and RE benchmarks"), §5 (experiments)
- 问题：论文标题和 abstract 将贡献定位为 "Information Extraction"，涵盖 NER + RE，但 RE 实验仅在 SciERC 一个 benchmark 上进行（且 40% zero-F1）。NER 有 3 个 benchmark 跨难度梯度，RE 却缺乏类似设计。论文在正文中反复标注 "preliminary"（≥12 次），但标题、abstract 第 1–2 句和 Figure 1 caption 均未体现这一限定。Section 5.3 Table 3 直接报告 RE selection 结果作为核心证据之一。
- 为什么影响接收：Reviewer 看标题和 abstract 时会预期 balanced NER/RE coverage。单一 RE benchmark 不足以支撑 "Information Extraction" 级别的 claim。SciERC RE 的 40% zero-F1 率进一步削弱该 benchmark 的代表性——这更像是在 capability boundary 上测量，而非 "typical RE task"。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 将标题/abstract 显式限定为 "primarily NER, with preliminary RE evidence"；(2) 增加至少一个额外 RE benchmark（如 TACRED、DocRED、或 ACE05）；(3) 若无法增加数据集，则将 RE 结论完全移至附录并在 abstract 中删除 RE 相关的具体数字。

**N2** [critical] ε=0.05 "tied fraction" 阈值的 circularity
- 具体位置：Appendix §app:logprob_ties（line 499–500）, Table 11（ε sweep）, §5.2 footnote
- 问题：Appendix 声称 "the median within-instance LP range is only 0.041 nats—below the ε=0.05 threshold used throughout, providing data-driven justification for this cutoff rather than an arbitrary choice." 这是 circular reasoning：阈值 ε 的选择是为了让 median LP range 落在阈值以下。Table 11 的 ε sweep 显示 ε=0.05 恰好给出最强 p-value（p=0.004），而 ε=0.03 的 p=0.079 和 ε=0.10 的 p=0.034 都更弱。这暗示 ε=0.05 可能是通过 p-value optimization 选出的。
- 为什么影响接收：论文的核心定量发现——"60% tied, median range 0.041 nats"——直接依赖这个阈值。如果 ε 是 data-driven 的，那么 60% 这个数字就不是独立发现，而是 threshold tuning 的结果。ARR guidelines (R1) 明确标记 p-hacking/threshold optimization 为 problematic practice。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 用 pre-registered 或 literature-grounded ε（如 LP 的 numerical precision 或 FP16 最小可区分差异）替代 data-driven ε；(2) 报告 ε-free 的连续指标（如 median LP range 本身即可作为核心统计量，无需二值化）；(3) 如果保留 ε，至少明确承认 circularity 并在所有 tied-fraction 数字旁标注 "threshold-dependent"。

**N3** [critical] "LP compression is model/task intrinsic, not decoding artifact" 的因果推断被 RE reversal 削弱
- 具体位置：Abstract line 6, §6 ¶"Ablation: free-form decoding", Appendix §app:freeform_ablation Table 15 Panel B
- 问题：论文声称 free-form ablation "confirms NER compression is not an artifact of constrained decoding"（Abstract），但 RE 数据直接反驳了这一 claim：LP selection 在 constrained decoding 下为 −0.68 pp，在 free-form 下为 +1.69 pp（reversal of 2.37 pp）。这意味着 **至少对 RE 而言，constrained decoding 确实是 LP selection failure 的一个因素**。论文确实标注了 RE 为 preliminary，但 abstract 的措辞 "confirms NER compression is not an artifact of constrained decoding" 暗示了一个比实际证据更强的结论。
- 为什么影响接收：Abstract 是读者形成第一印象的地方。当前措辞可能让读者误以为 free-form ablation 全面排除了 constrained decoding 的影响，而实际上只对 NER 成立。RE 的 regime-dependent behavior 是论文的一个重要 nuance，不应被 abstract 的简化措辞掩盖。
- 建议修改方向：Abstract 改为 "A free-form decoding ablation confirms NER compression is not caused by constrained decoding; on RE, LP selection *reverses direction* under free-form decoding, suggesting regime-dependent behavior (preliminary, single benchmark)." 此外，Discussion §6 应更明确地讨论 RE reversal 对 "task-intrinsic" claim 的限制。

---

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1** [warning] Scale range (3B–8B) 过窄，不足以支撑 "task difficulty is the primary driver" 因果结论
- 具体位置：§5.4 line 120, Conclusion line 6
- 问题：论文在 main text 中声称 "within the 3B–8B range tested across two model families, task difficulty appears to be the primary driver of the gap"，这是一个强因果推断。3B→8B 的 scale range 极为有限——模型容量差异仅 ~2.5x。70B+ 模型可能产生质性不同的 LP distributions（如 better-calibrated probabilities），从根本上改变 compression 特性。Limitations 部分承认了这一点，但 main text 的 claim 语气过强。
- 建议：将 "task difficulty appears to be the primary driver" 弱化为 "task difficulty is a stronger predictor than model scale within the 3B–8B range tested"，并在 §5.4 加注 scale limitation caveat。

**W2** [warning] 3 seeds 对 stability claims 的统计效力不足
- 具体位置：Appendix §app:multiseed Table 8, §app:n_scaling Table 10 (Kendall's W)
- 问题：Kendall's W=1.000（3 seeds）不具信息量——5 个 signals 中只要所有 3 seeds 排序一致即 W=1，而 3 个观测的任何一致排序都会达到这个值。σ≤0.026 的估计基于 n=3，其 95% CI 非常宽（population σ 可能高达 ~0.065 假设 χ² distribution）。论文声称 "signal ranking is stable across seeds" 时 overclaims 了统计证据的强度。
- 建议：(1) 增加至少 5–10 seeds（推理 cost 较低，不需重训）；(2) 或者弱化 stability 措辞为 "rankings were consistent across the 3 seeds tested" 而非 "stable"。

**W3** [warning] Greedy baseline 命名混淆 + 基线 variance 未充分讨论
- 具体位置：§3.2 line 60, Table 3 footnote
- 问题：论文的 "greedy" 实际是 T=1.0 的单次采样，而非 argmax (T→0) decoding。在 IE/NLG 文献中，"greedy" 通常指 argmax decoding。这个命名选择可能导致误读。更重要的是，greedy baseline 本身有 sampling variance（2-seed mean±σ 在 Table 3 中显示 σ=0.001），但论文未讨论使用 T=1.0 random sample 而非 argmax 作为基线的 motivation。如果 argmax 比 random sample 更好，则 gap 更大；如果更差，则论文高估了 gap。
- 建议：(1) 使用 "single-sample" 或 "random sample" 替代 "greedy"；(2) 增加 argmax (T=0) baseline 作为对照。

**W4** [warning] 缺少信号组合实验
- 具体位置：§6 Discussion, §7 Conclusion
- 问题：论文评估了 5 个独立信号，但未测试任何信号组合策略（如 LP + SJ 加权、LP ranking restricted to high-VC instances、或简单的 linear combination）。虽然论文的核心贡献是诊断而非解决 gap，但缺少组合实验让读者无法判断 gap 是否因为单信号 insufficient，还是因为信号本身就不包含足够的 discriminative information。非 tied LP subset 的 +2.9 pp gain（§6, p=0.004）暗示组合策略（如 VC 筛选 + LP 排序）可能有效。
- 建议：增加至少一个 simple combination baseline（如 "LP ranking among top-50% VC instances"），或明确讨论为什么 combination 不在 scope 内。

**W5** [warning] Gold-empty filtering 在 CoNLL 上比例过高（20.2%），交叉数据集可比性受影响
- 具体位置：Appendix §app:robustness line 31–32, §3.2 line 56
- 问题：CoNLL 过滤了 20.2% 的 empty-gold instances（697/3453），而 SciERC 仅 4.0%（22/551）。这意味着 CoNLL 的 correlation 分析在 substantially different population 上进行。Empty-gold 的高比例可能反映了 CoNLL 中大量无实体句子（新闻文本特征），但也意味着 CoNLL 的 ρ 数字可能与 SciERC 不直接可比，因为 population difficulty distributions 不同。
- 建议：(1) 报告 CoNLL full-set（含 empty-gold）的 ρ 作为对照；(2) 讨论 filtering rate 差异对跨数据集比较的影响。

**W6** [warning] Qwen3-8B SciERC thinking token confound 的 "CoNLL control" 论证逻辑薄弱
- 具体位置：Appendix §app:thinking_token ¶"CoNLL control group"
- 问题：论证逻辑是：如果 thinking token 导致 LP compression，CoNLL（无 thinking token）应有更低的 tied fraction。但 CoNLL tied fraction 更高（86.8% vs 60.3%），因此排除 thinking token 假说。然而 CoNLL 和 SciERC 的 task difficulty 完全不同——CoNLL 是 easy task（F1≈0.91），高 tied fraction 更可能是因为输出多样性低（57–88% identical outputs, Table 7），而非 LP 本身被 compress。这个 confound（task difficulty vs. thinking token）未被分离。
- 建议：(1) 重训 SciERC checkpoint without enable_thinking=True 作为 clean control（如果 compute 允许）；(2) 或者弱化 CoNLL control 的证据力度，更多依赖前两个论证（LP shift magnitude 和 constant prefix cancellation），它们更有说服力。

---

## 小问题（不影响接收）

- Table 3 的 NER F1 报告为 "2-seed mean±σ"，但论文其他部分使用 3 seeds。为什么 selection 表只用 2 seeds？应说明原因或统一为 3 seeds。
- §3.2 line 56：correlation 分析排除 empty gold 但 selection 保留 full set（n=529 vs n=551）。两个 evaluation 的 population 不同，应在 experiments section（而非仅 appendix）明确说明。
- Figure 1 caption 中 "Right: instance-level signals assign identical scores to all candidates" 仅适用于 4 个 instance-level signals，LP 作为 per-sample signal 不适用；caption 应更精确。
- 引用格式：`\cite` vs `\citet` 使用不一致——Introduction line 3 用 `\citep{wang2023selfconsistency}` 但同行 line 7 用 `\cite{wang2023selfconsistency}`。
- 引用验证：3 条 bib entries 未在 OpenAlex 索引中找到（hobelsberger2025systematic, lightman2024verify, venktesh2025trust），均为知名预印本/会议论文，可能为索引延迟，非引用错误。

---

## Questions to Authors

1. ε=0.05 的选择是否先于 LP range 分析确定？如果是 post-hoc，请提供 ε-free 的核心指标（如 continuous LP range distribution）作为补充。
2. 为什么 selection analysis 在 Table 3 使用 2 seeds 而非与 QE 分析一致的 3 seeds？
3. 是否考虑过 LP + consistency signal 的组合策略？例如在 high-VC instances 上使用 LP ranking。
4. Free-form RE reversal 是否在不同 temperature 下也成立？当前仅测试了 T=1.0。
5. 如果增加 TACRED 或 ACE05 作为 RE benchmark，是否预计 RE conclusions 会有质性变化？

---

## Missing References

- **Ye et al. (2023)** "Selfee: Iterative Self-Revising LLM Empowered by Self-Feedback Generation" — 相关于 self-refinement for structured outputs
- **Huang et al. (2024)** "Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet" — 对 self-assessment 能力的限制有直接相关性
- 论文引用了 Eikema & Aziz (2022) 的 MBR，但未引用 **Fernandes et al. (2022)** "Quality-Aware Decoding for Neural Machine Translation" 中 MBR 在 structured prediction 的早期讨论

---

## 主要优势

- **统计方法论在同类工作中属上乘**：Bootstrap CI、permutation test、TOST equivalence testing（含外部锚点和 circularity 讨论）、Fisher combined p、Bonferroni correction，形成了完整的统计证据链。
- **三指标框架（ρ, AUROC, selection F1）的 dissociation** 是重要的方法论贡献，揭示了单指标评估的陷阱。
- **极其详尽的 appendix**（15 个 section），几乎每个 claim 都有 robustness check，远超该领域的平均水平。
- **诚实的 hedging**：RE 标注 "preliminary" 12+ 次，Limitations section 全面且具体。
- **Matched training protocol**（Table 9）消除了跨模型比较中的训练 confound。
- **LP compression 的诊断分析**（CDF、ε sweep、non-tied subset、free-form ablation、verbalized confidence comparison）是系统性的，构成论文最有洞察力的贡献。

---

现在将报告发送给 Review Director。

content.thinking:
Let me carefully go through Reviewer 2's comments and respond to each one based on what I've read in the paper. I need to assess each point independently and decide whether I agree or disagree, citing specific evidence from the paper.

Let me go through each point:

**N1: "Instance-level signals fail by construction" is definitional, not empirical**

This is an interesting critique. R2 argues that the fact that instance-level signals can't do per-sample selection is definitional/tautological, not an empirical finding. Let me think about this...

The paper does say "fail by construction" explicitly. 

The "metric dissociation" contribution is really about showing that ρ, AUROC, and selection F1 decouple empirically — that a signal can have good quality estimation but poor selection performance. While the instance-level limitation is indeed definitional for most signals, the actual quantification of how much these metrics diverge (like the 13.3 point gap) is an empirical result that requires data to demonstrate. R2 has a point that the framing could be clearer about what's definitional versus what's empirically discovered.

On the incremental contributions over Yao et al., the SJ versus EM comparison shows only marginal gains (Δρ=+0.065 with a bootstrap CI that barely clears zero), which R2 correctly flags. The selection analysis is a negative result but an important one that fills a gap in prior work. The WNUT-17 difficulty gradient reveals signal collapse across the dataset, which provides useful insights about where these methods break down.

I think R2 is undervaluing the selection analysis here — the core novelty is showing that correlation doesn't necessarily translate to selection performance. The LP compression findings (median 0.041 nats with 60% tied outputs) and the MBR failures within and across instances are genuinely new observations, and the free-form ablation adds causal weight to the claims. So while the incremental contribution is more substantial than R2 suggests, the paper could frame these contributions more sharply.

On the "preliminary" language, I see the point about repetition being distracting, though I also recognize the value in being transparent about limitations. It's partly a stylistic choice, and the paper is making the right call by being honest. The LP compression analysis does lack a mechanistic explanation for why this happens, which is a fair critique.

Regarding Spearman ρ as the primary QE metric, I think this is actually well-justified — it's the standard choice for measuring monotonic correlation between continuous signals and outcomes, rank-based so it handles non-linearity robustly, and AUROC is also reported. This particular critique feels somewhat weak to me.

Now I'm checking the missing references — conformal structured prediction is definitely relevant, but I need to verify whether those 2026-dated papers actually exist before I can agree they should be cited. Slim-SC and thought pruning work also seems worth including since it relates to test-time scaling.

The paper proposes a general framework for conformal prediction in the structured prediction setting, modifying existing conformal prediction algorithms to output structured prediction sets that implicitly represent sets of labels.

## "Beyond Confidence: Rethinking Self-Assessments for Performance Prediction in LLMs"

The paper was submitted on May 8, 2026, with authors Sree Bhattacharyya, Samarth Khanna, Leona Chen, Lucas Craig, Tharun Dilliraj, and James Z. Wang.

**Research Focus:**

The paper addresses how Large Language Models (LLMs) can achieve reliable self-assessment, which is critical in many applications. While assessment methods have evolved from using probabilistic correctness estimates to eliciting verbalized confidence, confidence has been shown to be an inconsistent and overoptimistic predictor of model correctness.

**Main Approach:**

The authors draw on cognitive appraisal theory, a framework from human psychology that decomposes self-evaluation into multiple components, to propose a multidimensional perspective on model self-assessment.

**Key Findings:**

Competence-related appraisal dimensions, particularly effort and ability, consistently match or outperform confidence across most settings, and effort yields less overoptimistic estimates that remain stable across model sizes. Furthermore, the most informative dimension varies systematically with task characteristics: effort is most predictive for reasoning-intensive tasks, while ability and confidence dominate on retrieval-oriented tasks.

I found the arxiv paper 2603.08999 titled "Learning When to Sample: Confidence-Aware Self-Consistency for Efficient LLM Chain-of-Thought Reasoning".

Here are the key details:

**Paper Information:**
- Submitted on 9 Mar 2026 (v1), last revised 17 Mar 2026 (v2)
- Authors: Juming Xiong, Kevin Guo, Congning Ni, Chao Yan, Katherine Brown, Avinash Baidya, Xiang Gao, Bradley Malin, Zhijun Yin

**Summary:**
Large language models achieve strong reasoning performance through chain-of-thought reasoning, yet often generate unnecessarily long reasoning paths that incur high inference cost. Recent self-consistency-based approaches further improve accuracy but require sampling and aggregating multiple reasoning trajectories, leading to substantial additional computational overhead.

The paper introduces a confidence-aware decision framework that analyzes a single completed reasoning trajectory to adaptively select between single-path and multi-path reasoning. The framework is trained using sentence-level numeric and linguistic features extracted from intermediate reasoning states in the MedQA dataset and generalizes effectively to MathQA, MedMCQA, and MMLU without additional fine-tuning.

**Results:**
Experimental results show that the proposed method maintains accuracy comparable to multi-path baselines while using up to 80% fewer tokens.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Slim-SC:

## Overview

Slim-SC: Thought Pruning for Efficient Scaling with Self-Consistency is a paper by Colin Hong, Xu Guo, Anand Chaanan Singh, Esha Choukse, and Dmitrii Ustiugov presented at EMNLP 2025.

## Problem and Solution

Standard Self-Consistency (SC) improves LLM reasoning but is computationally expensive and slow due to generating many full reasoning chains. The analysis reveals that correct and incorrect chains form distinct semantic clusters, with incorrect chains often being highly redundant.

Slim-SC is a dynamic thought-pruning method that identifies and removes these redundant chains step-by-step during generation based on their semantic similarity.

## Performance Results

The method achieves significant efficiency gains, reducing end-to-end latency by up to 45% (on GPQA) and token usage by up to 32% (on AIME-2024), while also lowering mean KV Cache usage by 10pp, and crucially, these gains are achieved while maintaining or even slightly improving accuracy (+0.5pp on GPQA).

## Technical Approach

Slim-SC is a step-wise pruning strategy that identifies and removes redundant chains using inter-chain similarity at the thought level. The paper was published in the Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing in Suzhou, China.

Good, I've verified all 4 missing references suggested by Reviewer 2. They all exist. Now let me compose my cross-response.

Let me go through each point:

**N1: "Instance-level signals fail by construction" is definitional**
I partially agree. The "by construction" part IS definitional. But the metric dissociation (that high ρ doesn't translate to selection) requires empirical demonstration. The framing could be improved, but the contribution isn't purely definitional. I'll REBUT with nuance.

Actually, thinking more carefully — R2 has a strong point. The paper lists "Metric dissociation" as Contribution 1, but the dissociation for 4/5 signals is trivially explained by the instance-level nature. The only non-trivial dissociation is for LP. 

Since the LP compression finding is already Contribution 2, Contribution 1 is mostly just restating what's definitional about instance-level signals. I'll partially AGREE with this critique.

**N2: RE single benchmark — same as my N1**
[AGREE] — I raised the same issue.

**N3: Incremental over Yao et al. (2026)**
This is more nuanced. The SJ vs EM improvement is marginal at Δρ=+0.065, but the structural versus LP gap shows a more substantial difference of Δρ=+0.155 in Table 6. The selection analysis functions more as a negative result, which complicates the incrementality claim.

R2 seems to dismiss this, but the real insight is the gap itself — Yao et al. only examined whether signals correlate with quality, while this work shows they correlate but fail at selection time. That distinction matters for the test-time scaling community. I'll REBUT this point.

The WNUT-17 collapse is informative about where the signal boundaries break down.

**W1: "Preliminary" too frequent**
[AGREE] partially — the transparency is valuable, but using it 12+ times feels repetitive and could be consolidated.

**W2: LP compression lacks mechanistic explanation**
[AGREE] — fair point. The paper demonstrates compression happens and rules out constrained decoding for NER, but doesn't explain the underlying mechanism.

**W3: Missing conformal prediction discussion**
[REBUT] — Conformal prediction constructs prediction sets with coverage guarantees, which is fundamentally different from selecting a single best output. The connection is high-level (both address uncertainty in structured outputs) but doesn't directly apply to the paper's core task.

**W4: 3B-8B scale**
[AGREE] — same concern as W1.

**W5: Spearman ρ as primary QE metric**
[REBUT] — Spearman ρ is the standard for monotonic rank correlation because it's rank-based, doesn't assume normality, and directly measures whether higher signals predict higher quality. The paper also reports AUROC for binary discrimination, providing complementary perspectives.

The paper actually demonstrates that ρ and AUROC can diverge (§5.1), which strengthens the case for reporting both metrics rather than relying on either alone.

On the missing references: I'd agree that Conformal Structured Prediction and "Beyond Confidence" are relevant additions to related work, especially the latter given its recent focus on verbalized confidence limitations. The other two papers on adaptive sampling and efficient scaling are tangentially related but primarily target discrete-answer tasks, which the paper already distinguishes from structured information extraction.

四篇缺失引用均已验证存在。现在逐条回应 Reviewer 2。

---

## 交叉回应 Reviewer 2

### Must-Fix 问题

**[REBUT] R2-N1: "Instance-level signals fail by construction" 是 definitional observation，不应算作 empirical contribution**

R2 的批评部分成立但过度延伸。"四个 instance-level signals 无法 rank candidates" 确实是构造性的（definitional），论文自身也承认了这一点（Section 5.2: "instance-level signals assign identical scores to all candidates per input and cannot rank outputs by construction"）。但 Contribution 1（"Metric dissociation"）的核心不是这个 definitional observation，而是 **三个评估指标（ρ, AUROC, selection F1）在实证中的 decoupling**——这需要数据来展示。具体地：

- Table 1 中 EM 在 CoNLL 上 AUROC 最高（0.816）但 ρ 不是最高（0.451 vs VC 0.424）——这不是构造性的
- Appendix §app:verbalized_confidence 中 VerbConf ρ > LP（0.297 vs 0.205）但 selection 最差（−2.45 pp）——per-sample signal 之间的 QE-selection dissociation 不是 definitional
- Table 4（WNUT-17）中 LP full-set ρ = −0.410 但 conditional ρ = 0.350——这种 inversion 是 empirical finding

但我同意 **framing 可改进**。当前 Contribution 1 混合了 definitional 前提和 empirical 发现。建议作者将 instance-level/per-sample 区分移至 §3（Problem Formulation）作为前提，将 Contribution 1 重新聚焦为 "the three evaluation metrics decouple empirically, with implications for signal selection methodology."

关于 Eikema & Aziz (2025) 的重叠：论文的 MBR 分析确实与 structured MBR 发现一致，但论文提供了 **IE-specific 的具体 failure mode**——utility correlates across but not within instances（§6, Appendix §app:mbr_discussion）。Eikema et al. 讨论的是 bag-of-unit mismatch 的一般性降级，而本文定位了 structured IE 的 specific failure pattern。增量贡献存在，但应更清晰地 differentiate。

---

**[AGREE] R2-N2: RE 结论仅基于 SciERC 单一 benchmark 且 40% zero-F1 rate**

与我的 N1 完全一致。Title/abstract scope 与 RE 证据不匹配是本文最主要的 overclaim。

---

**[REBUT] R2-N3: 与 Yao et al. (2026) 的增量贡献不够清晰**

R2 低估了 selection analysis 的贡献价值。

(a) **SJ vs EM**：R2 正确指出 Δρ=+0.065 仅 marginal significance（Bootstrap CI [+0.003, +0.130]，Table 6）。但更重要的比较是 **structural vs LP**：SJ−LP Δρ=+0.155，CI [+0.074, +0.234]，clearly significant。Yao et al. (2026) 仅使用 surface-level EM/FK-type signals，未评估结构化匹配（SJ, VC），也未评估 LP。本文展示 structural > LP 对 QE 是 robust finding。

(b) **Selection analysis 作为 "core negative result"**：Yao et al. 止步于 correlation，完全没有回答 "correlation 能否转化为 selection" 这个问题。而这恰恰是 test-time compute scaling 社区最关心的问题（Snell et al. 2025, Brown et al. 2024 的核心假设是 more samples → better selection）。本文的 correlation-selection gap 证明了这个假设在 structured IE 中不成立，并给出了 mechanistic explanation（LP compression + MBR across/within failure）。**Negative results 在 ARR guidelines 中被明确保护**（H6: "The bias towards publishing only positive results is a known problem"）。

(c) **WNUT-17 collapse**：虽然 "all signals collapse" 可能不 surprising，但 Table 4 的 LP full-set/conditional inversion（ρ = −0.410 → +0.350）和 VC 的 boundary-driven inflation（full ρ=0.724, conditional ρ=0.038）提供了具体的 diagnostic insight，这不仅是 "collapse" 而是展示了不同 failure modes。

总体：增量贡献的 combined novelty 足够，但作者应在 Introduction 中更明确地 tabulate 与 Yao et al. 的差异。

---

### Should-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R2-W1: "Preliminary" 标注过于频繁（≥11次）**

同意这是 presentation issue。诚实的 scope 限定是优点（见我的 Strengths），但 12+ 次 "preliminary" 确实让读者产生 "那为什么还要报告" 的印象。建议：(1) 在首次出现时（Abstract 或 §1）给出一次完整说明："RE conclusions rest on SciERC alone and should be considered preliminary"；(2) 后续用简洁标记（如表格中的 † 符号）替代 inline "(preliminary)"。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W2: LP compression 缺乏 mechanistic explanation**

这是论文的一个实质性空白。论文展示了 LP compression 的存在（median range 0.041 nats, Table 9）、排除了 constrained decoding 作为 NER 原因（Appendix Table 15）、并展示了 verbalized confidence 也有类似压缩（Appendix §app:verbalized_confidence, mean 8.58/10），但没有解释 **为什么** token-averaged log-probability 在 within-instance 维度上如此 compressed。

可能的 mechanistic hypotheses（论文均未探索）：
- Token-level averaging 平滑了 per-token LP variance，尤其当大部分 tokens 是 schema-enforced 的（如 JSON 括号、key names），只有少量 value tokens 有实际 variance
- Constrained decoding 下有效 vocabulary 缩小，softmax 集中于少数 valid tokens
- Sequence-level calibration vs token-level calibration 的 mismatch

论文至少应讨论这些 hypotheses，即使不做实验验证。

---

**[REBUT] R2-W3: 缺少对 conformal prediction / set-valued uncertainty 的讨论**

Conformal structured prediction（Feldman et al., ICLR 2025）解决的问题与本文 fundamentally 不同。Conformal prediction 构建具有 coverage guarantee 的 **prediction sets**（输出一组可能的 labels），其目标是 "the true label is in the set with probability ≥ 1−α"。本文的 best-of-N selection 目标是从 N 个 point predictions 中选一个最好的——这是 point selection 而非 set construction。

两个问题在 uncertainty quantification 层面有 high-level connection（都关心 structured output 的不确定性），但方法论和目标完全不同。在 Related Work §2 中简要提及一句足矣（"Conformal methods construct prediction sets with coverage guarantees rather than selecting among point predictions"），但 R2 要求的 detailed discussion 不必要，可能会 dilute focus。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W4: 3B-8B 规模限制**

与我的 W1 一致。Main text 的 causal claim 语气过强。

---

**[REBUT] R2-W5: Spearman ρ 作为 primary QE metric 缺乏 justification**

Spearman ρ 是 quality estimation 的标准 metric choice，在 uncertainty estimation 文献中广泛使用（Kuhn et al. 2023, Kadavath et al. 2022——论文自身引用）。其优势是：(1) rank-based，对非线性 monotonic 关系鲁棒；(2) 不假设正态分布；(3) 直接度量 "higher signal → higher quality" 的 ordinal relationship，这正是 QE 的定义。

更重要的是，**论文并非只用 ρ**。论文同时报告了 AUROC（binary discrimination）和 selection F1（downstream task performance），且正是通过展示三者的 decoupling 来论证单指标评估的不足（Contribution 1）。如果论文只用 ρ，R2 的批评成立；但论文的 three-metric framework 本身就是对 "single metric" 问题的回应。

R2 可能的 concern 是 Spearman ρ 对 F1 分布中的 floor/ceiling effects 不鲁棒（如 WNUT-17 的 52% zero-F1 会 inflate ρ through boundary effects）。论文用 conditional analysis（non-zero F1）处理了这个问题（Table 4, Figure 3）。

---

### 缺失引用

**[AGREE] #1 Conformal Structured Prediction (ICLR 2025)**
已验证存在。虽然如上述 W3 所论，方法论上 tangential，但在 Related Work §2 ¶"Uncertainty estimation" 中简要提及是合理的。

**[AGREE] #2 "Beyond Confidence" (arxiv 2605.07806, May 2026)**
已验证存在。该论文从 cognitive appraisal theory 出发，发现 effort/ability 等维度可优于 confidence 做 performance prediction——与本文的 verbalized confidence failure（Appendix §app:verbalized_confidence, mean 8.58/10）直接相关。应在 Discussion 或 Appendix K 中引用。

**[REBUT] #3 "Learning When to Sample" (arxiv 2603.08999, March 2026)**
已验证存在。但该论文处理 **discrete-answer CoT reasoning**（MedQA, MathQA），使用 single-trajectory confidence 决定是否需要 multi-path——这正是本文 Introduction 明确区分的 "discrete answer" setting。论文已引用了同类工作（Feng et al. 2025, Wang & Make 2025, Kim et al. 2026 ReaSC），coverage 充分。该引用属于 nice-to-have 而非 missing。

**[REBUT] #4 Slim-SC / Thought Pruning (EMNLP 2025)**
已验证存在。同样处理 discrete-answer self-consistency 的 **efficiency** 问题（pruning redundant chains），与本文关注 structured IE 的 quality estimation / selection failure 问题不同。论文 Related Work §2 已引用多篇 efficiency-oriented self-consistency 工作（Taubenfeld et al. 2025 CISC, Kang et al. 2025 Self-Certainty, ReaSC 2026）。Slim-SC 属于同一类别，非 critical missing reference。

---

现在将回应发送给 Director。
